items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: Conte Candoli and a few other brass players... When they got to Buffalo they needed two trumpet players... So I went out and Conte decided not to come back... that's how I stayed on the band.

ctx.x: Sam, how did the thing with Kenton come about?

That was another strange story. I mean a bus had an accident on the Pennsylvania Turnpike coming to Buffalo to perform. And when they got to Buffalo, Conte Candoli and a few other brass players had hit the seat in front you know, and they wiped their chops out. And Conte’s wife was pregnant and she cracked her back, her vertebra, and so he had to leave the band. When they got to Buffalo they needed two trumpet players, so I got the call because I could play high notes. They called the union, you know, said, “You…
Stranger things than that have happened.
